summary: Tested Fee rules auto-populating from the fee type, including multi-country rules and extend_type. New file tests/test_r15_fee_rule_scope.py: 12 of 13 pass. (1) Every fee type has a categories list, and PATCH /fee-types/{id} saves categories (checked with GET). (2) Rule country: countries [kz, IN] saves as country=MULTI with countries=[IN,KZ]; one country saves as that code; no country saves as ALL; the old payload with only country=KZ still works. (3) GET /emd-masters?country=IN returns the MULTI and ALL rules and no KZ-only rule. (4) Fee type limited to KZ: a rule for [KZ,IN] returns 422 without extend_type and 200 with it, and IN is added to the fee type. Selected categories behave the same way, and PATCH with extend_type works too. (5) find_rule: a registration rule for [XT,XU] gives a fee of 77 to an XU vendor adding an extra category (via GET /vendor/categories/fee-quote). The country rule beats an ALL rule (11); after the multi rule is deleted, the quote falls back to 11. FAIL: if extend_type=true and the rule then fails validation (e.g. no slabs), the fee type is still changed. Regression: r10 33/33, r11 27/27, r12 14/14 and r13 17/17 pass when each file runs on its own with -n 0. Running r11 and r13 in one session fails 3 r13 tests; this is a problem in the tests' own event-loop setup, not in the app. UI (admin Masters): picking a fee type limited to KZ plus 1 category hides the All/Some radios and pre-ticks KZ and the category. Ticking India and a new category shows amber '(new)' chips and the emd-extend-note. Save shows the toast 'Fee rule created · 2 added to fee type ...', the fee type gets both, and the rule row lists 'India, Kazakhstan · cat1, cat2'. Edit reopens with the saved values. The EMD type (all countries) shows the radios with All checked, and 'Specific' shows the picker. Fee types: Categories=Selected shows the ft-categories picker; save works, the row shows 'Categories: ...' and edit pre-fills it. All TEST_ data was deleted. The 10 fee types and 2 original rules were left unchanged.

minor.issue: extend_type adds countries/categories to the fee type with $addToSet BEFORE validate_rule_against_type runs. If validation then fails (no slabs, wrong calc, amount <= 0) or PATCH targets a missing rule id (404), the fee type has still been changed. Fix: validate first using a copy of ft with the merged lists, and write the fee type only after the rule is saved.

minor.endpoint: _check_fee_type extend for category_scope=selected with an empty categories list
minor.issue: Fee types such as tender_management and premium_subscription are 'selected' with [] categories, which today means any category passes. The UI marks every ticked category as '(new)' and sends extend_type=true. The first rule saved therefore turns the type into a fixed list, and any later rule with a different category is rejected unless it extends the type again. This may be intended, but it quietly changes behaviour.
List items are not checked for length or format (country has max_length 5, countries does not). Junk codes can be stored and added to fee types.

issues: Multi-country rules appear as 'NAME · MULTI' in the rule dropdown; show the country names instead.
Countries are shown as raw codes ('Countries: KZ, IN'), while Fee rules shows names.

A legacy rule with country=ALL whose fee type is limited to selected countries opens in 'all' mode. The radios are hidden for selected-scope types and the picker only shows in 'some' mode, so no country can be ticked and save returns 422.
Switching Categories back to 'All' does not clear form.categories, so stale categories are saved on a type whose scope is all.

action_items: Move the fee-type $addToSet in _check_fee_type to after validation and after a successful insert/update, so a failed request does not change the fee type (test_failed_validation_does_not_extend encodes this).
Optional: in openEdit, if the fee type's country_scope is 'selected', force country_mode='some' (prefilled from ft.countries), so legacy ALL rules can still be edited.
Optional: show country names for MULTI in the calculator dropdown and in the Fee types row; clear categories when category_scope switches to all.
critical_code_review_comments: _check_fee_type changes the fee type before validation: the write is not atomic and has side effects on failure.
extend_type is always true in the UI payload; the backend only extends selected-scope types, which is fine.
country_q uses $or on country/countries; legacy rules without a countries field still match through country. OK.
seed_data_creation: Temporary TEST_R15 fee types/rules (and test_r15ui fee types via Mongo for the UI); all deleted. The test vendor's country and business_categories were restored by the fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest tests/test_r15_fee_rule_scope.py -n 0. The 1 failing test encodes the extend-before-validate bug. Run r10-r13 one file at a time: r11 + r13 in one session breaks r13's asyncio.new_event_loop find_rule test (motor loop binding). Admin UI login: /admin/login, wait about 4s before filling admin-login-email/password, then wait about 5s. Fee rules tab: masters-tab-emd_rules. Fee types tab: masters-tab-fee_types. The category picker inside Fee types reuses the emd-category-* testids.
